result.topic_en: Euler finishes remarks on the arbitrary comparison curve BN (its tangent must never be normal to the axis) and begins §37, which interprets the first part of the variation found in §14 as the integral term over the curve from A to M.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 57

requirimus. Praeterea tamen notandum eſt, in curva illa arbitraria B N nusquam tangentem ad axem A P normalem eſſe debere, quia hoc modo diuiſio illorum interuallorum turbaretur. Atque nunc euidens eſt, non ſolum interualla Y $v$ eſſe infinite parva, ſed etiam tangentes in punctis Y et $v$ infinite parum a parallelismo deficere.

37. His circa ipſam quaeſtionis propoſitionem annotatis, contemplemur nunc accuratius quoque ſolutionem ſupra inuentam, eiusque ſingulas partes, vt quid quaelibet earum innuat et ad quemnam vſum ſit transferenda perſpicue intelligamus; ſolutionem autem in §. 14. datam hic contemplabimur. Statim igitur conſideremus primam variationis ibi inuentae partem, quae hac formula integrali continetur.

$dt\int dx\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)\left(N-\left(\frac{dP}{dx}\right)+\left(\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}\right)-\left(\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}\right)+\left(\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}\right)-\text{etc.}\right)$

cuius integratio ita capi debet, vt in ipſo termino initiali A euaneſcat, qua conditione conſtans arbitraria determinatur, quod ſi ergo in ſingulis punctis X Y haec formula applicata intelligatur, aggregatum omnium iſtarum formularum elementarium ab initio A vsque ad terminum M extenſum praebebit primam partem variationis quaeſitae, atque hic quidem in Figura perſpicuum eſt, ſpatiolum Y $v$ exprimere incrementum applicatae $y$ a ſola variabili $t$ oriundum ita vt ſit Y $v = dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$.

Tom. XVI. Nou. Comm. H 38.

[margin:] Explicatio partis primae in variatione.

items.quote: in curva illa arbitraria B N nusquam tangentem ad axem A P normalem eſſe debere, quia hoc modo diuiſio illorum interuallorum turbaretur
items.english: In that arbitrary curve BN the tangent must nowhere be normal to the axis AP, because in that case the division of those intervals would be disturbed.

items.quote: non ſolum interualla Y $v$ eſſe infinite parva, ſed etiam tangentes in punctis Y et $v$ infinite parum a parallelismo deficere
items.english: Not only are the intervals Yv infinitely small, but the tangents at the points Y and v also deviate infinitely little from being parallel.

items.quote: contemplemur nunc accuratius quoque ſolutionem ſupra inuentam, eiusque ſingulas partes, vt quid quaelibet earum innuat et ad quemnam vſum ſit transferenda perſpicue intelligamus
items.english: Let us now examine more carefully the solution found above and each of its parts, so that we may clearly understand what each of them signifies and to what use it is to be applied.

items.quote: aggregatum omnium iſtarum formularum elementarium ab initio A vsque ad terminum M extenſum praebebit primam partem variationis quaeſitae
items.english: The sum of all these elementary formulas, extended from the beginning A to the end M, will give the first part of the variation sought.

items.quote: ſpatiolum Y $v$ exprimere incrementum applicatae $y$ a ſola variabili $t$ oriundum ita vt ſit Y $v = dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$
items.english: The small segment Yv expresses the increment of the ordinate y arising from the variable t alone, so that Yv = dt (dy/dt).
